task_instance: Decompose the sample ShopFast e-commerce monolith into microservices: define service boundaries, choose synchronous REST vs asynchronous event communication, design a Saga for the distributed checkout transaction, and specify resilience patterns (circuit breaker, retry/backoff, bulkhead, timeouts).
evidence: Read the skill SKILL.md and its references/details.md (both present next to the skill; details.md gives worked patterns for decomposition, API gateway, REST+retry, Kafka event bus, Saga, and circuit breaker). Chose a representative instance and created a realistic sample input monolith (input_monolith.md) describing a Django/Postgres online store with its modules and pain points. Produced the skill's core deliverable as text: microservices_design.md, a full architecture design applying every core pattern the skill names - a database-per-service boundary table for 8 services with DDD subdomain classification, Strangler Fig migration order, a synchronous-vs-asynchronous communication plan, an orchestration Saga with a 4-step/compensation table and a text state machine (inventory reserved before payment to remove the paid-but-out-of-stock bug), and resilience patterns (circuit breaker, timeouts, bounded pools, idempotent retry with backoff, bulkhead, graceful degradation), plus a section mapping each design choice back to each stated monolith pain point. Also produced event_contracts.json: a well-formed JSON event envelope, six event schemas with producers/consumers and example payloads, and a saga_trace_example showing the payment-declined compensation path. Verified the deliverable by re-reading both files: the design addresses all three deliverables in the skill description (service boundaries, event-driven communication, resilience patterns) and the JSON is syntactically valid and internally consistent with the design's saga. This skill is design/documentation work whose deliverable is written text, which the office-assistant runtime (read/write/edit text files) fully supports; no code execution, binary output, network, credentials, or connectors were required.
